input.question: Those websites that don't let you navigate away from, close, or go to a different page.
input.ground_truth: Web browsers have a few features that allow webmasters to program things to happen when someone tries to leave. They are *intended* to be used for *good*; for example, you have an online word processor, and if you leave before saving your work, it can warn you that it will be lost. But they can also be used for *evil*. It massively pisses off users, so no reputable site would do it, but many sketchy sites have no reputation to lose, so they use it for one last chance to try to sell you something. You may have to click "no" a few times, but the people that make web browsers are aware of this tactic, and after a few they give you an option to ignore any further attempts by the site to keep you there.
